basis: The on-site 124 MW facility is genuine electric generation (gas turbine generators, N+1), not merely mechanical drive, and is not grid-fed - it clears the >50 MW GOGPT threshold and is well-documented in FERC docket CP17-178. As-designed captive power on an unbuilt facility still counts. No GOGPT record for this on-site plant appears to exist (only the unrelated pre-existing Nikiski Combined Cycle plant nearby) - reviewer should decide whether to stage a new proposed-status GOGPT entry.
mechanical_drive_note: Each of the 3 LNG trains has 2 refrigerant compression strings, each driven directly by a natural gas turbine (mechanical/shaft drive, no generator) - 6 turbines total, combined ~800,000 ISO horsepower for refrigeration compression. Separate from the 124 MW electric-generation plant; produces zero MWe. NOTE: the 800,000 ISO-hp figure could not be cleanly verified (see verification_log) and is reported as background, not as a cited claim.

basis: The 130 MW / 2-unit GOGPT record matches exactly the two 65 MW steam turbine generators confirmed as dedicated on-site electric generation in FERC CP13-113 and the Maryland PPRP fact sheet - genuine captive electricity generation, self-consumed, never exported. Clean case for flipping GOGPT captive False -> True.
mechanical_drive_note: Two GE Frame 7EA gas turbines directly drive (mechanical/shaft coupling) the two main LNG refrigerant-compressor trains, ~86 MW ISO shaft power each (~172 MW combined shaft). Separate from and additional to the 130 MW electric figure.

basis: Disclosed nameplate capacity (430 MW) from an executed EPC supply contract (primary/legal source) for six gas-turbine generators plus a steam-turbine generator - true electricity generation, not mechanical-drive-only and not grid-fed. Reviewer flag: the plant's own description covers both 'LNG facilities and port facilities' (i.e. also the wider SEZ/port), so it is PARTIALLY captive rather than 100% dedicated to the LNG train - still ADD-eligible per the partially-captive rule.

GOGPT tracks electricity generation with a nameplate MW, and the design documents describe exactly that: a dedicated 180 MW natural-gas-fired generator plant (industrial gas turbines driving generator sets, open-cycle) built specifically to power the LNG facility's own electrical loads. This is textbook captive electric generation, not mechanical drive and not grid-fed, so it qualifies for CaptiveGasPower on the LNG terminal side.
mechanical_drive_note: Design also included a fully SEPARATE set of mechanical-drive gas turbines: the two liquefaction trains' refrigerant compressors were to use gas turbine drivers (Frame 7) of approximately 160 MW shaft power per train (4 machines total for 2 trains, i.e. ~640 MW combined shaft power). These are NOT part of the 180 MW figure and do not generate electricity, so they are excluded from electric_mw. The 180 MW GOGPT entry corresponds only to the separate Frame-6-turbine electric generator plant, so the captive designation here rests on straightforward electricity generation, not on mechanical drive.

basis: AMIGO's own compressor drive is undetermined (could end up zero-MWe mechanical drive, or grid/utility-fed electric motors), and no on-site captive generator has been disclosed at any capacity. Nothing confirmed to add.
mechanical_drive_note: As of the mid-2026 EPC contract award, project documentation lists refrigerant-compressor prime movers as either 'large frame gas turbines or high voltage motors with variable speed drives' - an unresolved either/or, not a locked selection. No MW or turbine model disclosed for either option; the article notes cost ranges 'will tighten as technology and equipment selection are locked.'

basis: Andres power station (319 MW gas, confirmed against the AES 10-K's 329 MW combined gas+battery figure) is a merchant grid-connected generator selling under PPAs, not captive load of the terminal. Its GOGPT record is valid as stand-alone generation but must never be linked to the Andres terminal as CaptiveGasPower.

The onboard steam-turbine-generator sets (66 MW) and gas-turbine compressor drivers are integral shipboard equipment built into the FLNG vessels themselves, not a standalone onshore power-plant facility with its own site/address -- GOGPT tracks discrete power stations, and there is no such separate facility here to add. The CaptiveGasPower field on the LNG terminal record is the correct place to capture this, not a new GOGPT entry.
mechanical_drive_note: Hilli Episeyo's 4 liquefaction trains (Black & Veatch PRICO single-mixed-refrigerant) are each driven by a GE PGT25+G4 aeroderivative gas turbine directly mechanically coupled to a GE 2BCL centrifugal refrigerant compressor - shaft drive, no generator in this loop - per GE's own press release announcing the equipment order for the conversion (4 compression trains with PGT25+G4 drivers) and GE's PGT25 brochure (~34 MW class per unit), i.e. roughly 136 MW of shaft power across 4 trains, far above the >50 MW threshold. NO PUBLICLY SOURCED ELECTRIC GENERATION FIGURE EXISTS for this vessel, so electric_mw is deliberately left blank (see orchestrator note). MK II (Fuji LNG hull) will also license PRICO but its equipment order for Argentina is not yet publicly disclosed.

basis: The mechanical-drive Frame 5 turbines are shaft-power-only (zero MWe) and are DO-NOT-ADD material for a GOGPT generation record. However the same primary source confirms a genuine electricity-GENERATING plant on site (Solar Mars 100 gas-turbine generator sets on the complex's internal grid). Solar Mars 100 units are ~11 MW-ISO class and at least 4 were added for Train 4 alone on top of a pre-existing fleet for Trains 1-3, so >50 MW is plausibly met - but no source discloses the total unit count or aggregate nameplate MW for Atlantic LNG specifically, so this is a reviewer call (worth pursuing via EMA/CEC environmental filings) rather than a confident ADD.
mechanical_drive_note: Train 1: 6x GE Frame 5C gas turbines mechanically driving the propane/ethylene/methane refrigeration compressors (2 per circuit); upgraded 2003-04 to Frame 5/2D spec, raising output 13% to 43,700 hp (~32.6 MW shaft) per unit (~196 MW aggregate shaft for Train 1 alone). Trains 2 & 3: 6x Frame 5D each, 2 per refrigeration circuit. Train 4: 8x Frame 5D turbine/compressor sets (3 propane + 3 ethylene + 2 methane) per the Phillips Optimized Cascade 'Two-Trains-in-One' design; aero-derivative alternatives (Rolls-Royce Coberra, LM-2500+/LM-6000) were evaluated for Train 4 and rejected in favour of more Frame 5D units. All four trains use gas-turbine MECHANICAL DRIVE for liquefaction refrigeration. The operator describes the resulting fleet as ~28 GE Frame 5-class turbine-compressors, the largest such fleet in the world - reported as BACKGROUND only, not a cited value, because that page failed the verifier (see verification_log).

basis: No verified own-generation MW figure for Tango FLNG exists in any source found, and the unit is a small-scale barge (~0.5-0.6 mtpa, 69.5 MMscf/d feed) well below the scale where a >50 MW captive plant would typically be expected without confirmation -- GOGPT tracks confirmed electricity-generation nameplate capacity, and inventing a figure here would be a defect, not a finding. Separately, Solalban Energia is an already-tracked, independently owned/older plant with no relationship to this terminal.
mechanical_drive_note: Undisclosed. Exmar's own project pages and Eni's technical/press materials describe Tango FLNG as a non-propelled barge (built by Wison, delivered 2017) with ~69.5 MMscf/d feed-gas intake and ~0.5-0.6 mtpa liquefaction capacity, but none of the sources found (Exmar milestone pages, Eni press release/PDF, offshore-technology.com, marinelink.com, offshore-energy.biz) state the make/model/count of the onboard power-generation engines or a MW figure, electric or mechanical. Extensive searching (incl. under the barge's original name 'Caribbean FLNG') found no Wärtsilä-branded reference to this specific unit; could not confirm the premise that Wärtsilä supplied its engines.

basis: No on-site generation asset to track - grid consumer; only combustion equipment is emergency/standby diesel (excluded by fuel and by function).
No on-site electricity-generation plant is documented at all; the only figure found (30 MW total facility demand) is below threshold and of undetermined source (grid vs on-site).
No developer selected and no technical design published - nothing to base a GOGPT record on.

The captive basis is mechanical-drive gas turbines (shaft horsepower on the refrigerant compressors), which GOGPT does not track. The one on-site item that does generate electricity (Unit 71, house power) has no disclosed MW and reads as balance-of-plant auxiliary, not a distinct generating station. The neighbouring 324 MW Baja California III plant is confirmed NOT captive (wrong direction, different owner) - GEM's existing captive=False flag on it is correct and should not change.
mechanical_drive_note: ECA LNG Phase 1's single APCI C3MR liquefaction train is refrigerant-compressor-driven, not electric: DOE FE docket 18-144-LNG (which incorporates ASEA's environmental-authorization letter ASEA/UGI/DGGPI/0233/2017 as an exhibit) identifies dedicated gas turbines driving both refrigerant compressor trains by equipment tag - the MR refrigerant High/Medium-pressure compressor turbine (G1-3101) and the propane refrigerant compressor turbine (G1-3102) - fed by the plant's own high-pressure fuel-gas system. No manufacturer/model disclosed in sources reviewed. Air Products' 2021 technology-award release separately confirms the train uses 'fuel-efficient mechanical drivers' alongside its coil-wound heat exchangers, consistent with shaft (non-electric) drive.

basis: AES Colon (381 MW) and Gatun (670 MW) are merchant grid-connected generators selling to Panama's distribution companies under PPAs, exactly matching the GOGPT Tier-C priors. Their GOGPT records are valid stand-alone generation entries but must never be linked to Costa Norte as CaptiveGasPower - the relationship is already correctly recorded as PowerPlantsSupplied on the GEM terminal record.
Electric-motor drive on purchased Georgia Power grid electricity; only combustion units are backup-only and far below the >50 MW threshold.
Mystic is a GOGPT generation record in its own right (now retired), not captive power of the terminal; fuel flows terminal->plant.
Project is pre-FEED with no published power/drive design; there is no generating-capacity claim of any kind to evaluate for GOGPT at this stage.

No engineering description of any generation facility exists; project still pre-FID with technology and EPC selection incomplete. A GOGPT record requires a nameplate MW, which does not exist here even preliminarily.

No liquefaction, refrigeration compression or LNG storage per the governing DRBC docket, which affirmatively bars on-site manufacturing and LNG storage. A loading-only dock has no generation-scale load.
No generation technology or nameplate MW has ever been disclosed; project remains pre-FEED with financing/negotiation unresolved.
No nameplate MW or generation-equipment description has ever been published for this dormant proposal.

GOGPT's existing Nikiski cogeneration record (captive=False) is correct as-is with respect to Kenai LNG: HEA/AEEC-owned grid generation whose historic steam host was the fertilizer plant, not the terminal.
mechanical_drive_note: Original 1969 liquefaction plant used single-shaft GE Frame 5 gas turbines to directly (mechanically) drive the LNG refrigeration compressors - shaft power only, no generator. Two independent verified sources confirm 'Frame 5' direct-drive turbines at Kenai; neither yields a verifiable aggregate MW/bhp figure (a candidate 84,600 bhp / 63.1 MW figure FAILED independent verification and was dropped).

basis: No power-generation design evidence to base a GOGPT record on; the project is also currently shelved with no construction/EA approval on record.

A real, disclosed, sized (603 MW, 8-unit combined-cycle) generation asset whose sole purpose would be powering the terminal. But explicitly a temporary/contingent fallback that activates only if the BC Hydro interconnection slips; project is pre-FID; barges designed for removal within 5 years of activation. Reviewer call.
mechanical_drive_note: None - the FLNGs' main refrigerant compressor drives are electric motors in every scenario (grid-fed and barge-fed); no mechanical-drive gas turbines anywhere in the design.

basis: All confirmed on-site turbines are mechanical-drive-only, shaft-coupled to refrigeration compressors with no generator. No dedicated electricity-generation set is disclosed in the EAO GHG filing, the BCER air permit, or LNG Canada's own materials - the 'cogeneration' feature recovers waste heat for process heating, not electricity. GOGPT tracks nameplate generation MW; no such asset exists here.
mechanical_drive_note: 4x GE LMS100(-PB) aeroderivative gas turbines (2 per train, 2 trains in Phase 1), each ~105 MW simple-cycle at ISO per GE; LNG Canada's own BC EAO GHG Management Technical Data Report cites a tested output rating of 93.4 MW per unit as its emissions basis. Each turbine's free power turbine is coupled directly to a refrigerant compressor string - shaft power only, no generator. Aggregate Phase-1 mechanical shaft output ~374-420 MW; a 4-train build-out doubles to 8 turbines per the same filing.

basis: No power configuration for the Sevan Driller conversion was ever published, and the project was terminated (Nov 2023) before such detail would exist publicly.

electric_mw: 33 MW per built FLNG unit (3x ~11 MW Siemens SGT-400 simple-cycle); 66 MW across the two authorised units FLNG1+FLNG2
basis: The SGT-400 turbines are embedded facility/utility generation on a jackup platform, not a standalone separately-identifiable power station of the kind GOGPT tracks; the larger driver (LM6000PF+) is pure mechanical drive with zero MWe. LNG-side CaptiveGasPower(+ref) edit only.
mechanical_drive_note: 1x Baker Hughes LM6000PF+ gas-turbine-driven compressor per FLNG unit, mechanically driving the main IPSMR refrigerant compressor on the liquefaction platform (Pioneer II) - not a generator; shaft MW undisclosed in any verified source.

basis: GOGPT's captive=True flag on Wyalusing Energy Center is correct as a captive plant but MIS-ATTRIBUTED if read as an LNG-terminal relationship - its host is the Klondike data centre. GOGPT-side note for the memo, no LNG-side edit.
Stated design is electric-drive fed by purchased renewable/nuclear power; no engineering document, permit filing or turbine selection exists. Grid-fed electric drive is DO NOT ADD by definition.

The EcoElectrica power station (574 MW per the GOGPT Tier-C prior; regulatory filings independently show 507 MW original / 530 MW as of the 2020 restructuring - see status_or_data_issues) is a legitimate stand-alone merchant IPP selling to PREPA's grid, not captive load of the terminal. It may validly exist in GOGPT as its own generation record but must NEVER be linked to Penuelas as CaptiveGasPower - the true relationship is PowerPlantsSupplied, the reverse field.

Genuine electricity generation exists on-site (3x GE LM2500+ gas turbine-generators, confirmed by GE plus two trade-press corroborations) - a GOGPT-relevant asset type, not merely mechanical drive. But no Peru-specific nameplate MW is published anywhere found (generic LM2500+ ~30 MW each would put the 3-unit set near/above 50 MW, but that generic spec is NOT asserted as this site's rating). Reviewer should confirm nameplate MW via OSINERGMIN/COES registry or an EIA/ESIA equipment list before adding a GOGPT record.
mechanical_drive_note: 2x GE Frame 7 / MS7001 ('7EA') gas turbines drive 4 centrifugal refrigeration compressors for the single-train ConocoPhillips Optimized Cascade process (propane/ethylene/methane loops). Shaft MW not disclosed in any available source (7EA units are generically ~85 MW-class, but no Peru-specific figure is published) - reported as turbine count/model only.

basis: Pre-FEED/feasibility-study stage only; no generation technology or MW disclosed for the FLNG unit's own power system.

The captive element here is gas-turbine shaft power directly driving the refrigeration compressors (mechanical drive, no generator/MWe); GOGPT tracks electricity-generation capacity with a nameplate MW, and this design assumption produces no separate generating plant to add. The site's actual electricity demand is planned to be grid-supplied hydro (NL Power/Muskrat Falls), which is the opposite of captive and also not a GOGPT-trackable generation asset belonging to this project.
mechanical_drive_note: The project's Nov 2021 NL environmental-assessment registration states gas turbine drivers are ASSUMED (base case) for the refrigerant compressor drivers, with total shaft power for refrigeration compressors estimated at 120-140 MW (plus ~40 MW additional utility power demand) for the 4 MTPA single-train FLNG design. Critically, the same document explicitly flags that a driver-selection study (gas turbine mechanical drive vs. electric motor drive fed by the NL hydro grid) was deferred to a later engineering phase, so the final choice was NOT settled at last filing — hence yellow rather than green confidence despite this being a primary regulatory source.

basis: No GOGPT record exists for this site and none should be added on current evidence - no citable finding of a specific gas-fired generation installation, only an undocumented concept.

GOGPT's 'Mexico Pacific power station' (141 MW, 1 unit, 0.0 km, pre-construction, captive=True) is plausible in shape - Freeport LNG, which licenses the same Optimized Cascade process, uses electric-motor-driven compression fed by an on-site captive gas-fired plant, so a generation island at a same-technology remote site would fit. But NO independent primary or trade-press source confirming this specific 141 MW facility's existence, capacity, status or purpose could be found outside GEM's own database. REVIEWER CALL pending the ASEA MIA or a CRE generation permit.
mechanical_drive_note: No public source found specifying turbine count/model or shaft MW for the refrigeration compressors. The only power-related detail in primary/company material is diesel generation for temporary construction facilities (Techint EPC release), explicitly not the permanent design.

basis: The operating terminal is grid-fed (NB Power transmission line), which is a clean non-captive case; the cancelled export addition never had a published power design to evaluate. Nothing here corresponds to an on-site generating plant with a nameplate MW.
mechanical_drive_note: N/A for the operating regas terminal — vaporization is seawater/ambient heat exchange (submerged combustion / open-loop type), not a compressor-driven process, so no mechanical-drive question applies. The separate cancelled export/liquefaction addition never reached an engineering stage where compressor-driver technology was published.

basis: Cogeneracion Salina Cruz is captive to the PEMEX refinery, not to an LNG terminal. Its own captive=True flag is correct but must not be cross-linked to an LNG terminal's CaptiveGasPower.
Refinery-captive cogeneration 7 km away; must not be cross-linked to this terminal.

San Juan (PR) power station (840 MW, 6 units) and San Juan II (560 MW, pre-construction) are PREPA/grid-connected generation assets fed BY this terminal, not captive generators feeding it. Their GOGPT records stand on their own merits; the LNG-side relationship, if recorded at all, belongs in PowerPlantsSupplied, never CaptiveGasPower.
Grid-fed electric-motor liquefaction, no on-site electricity generation of any kind.
No design or generation-capacity information exists in the public record found; project has not progressed beyond the November 2022 MOU.

GOGPT's own captive flag on Solalban is already False, and independent corroboration confirms why: Solalban was purpose-built as a captive generator for Solvay/Unipar Indupa's petrochemical plant, not for TGS's gas transport or LNG operations. No source ties Solalban's output to Puerto Galvan, and TGS's own project materials describe no dedicated power source at all -- nothing here supports a GOGPT-to-terminal captive link in either direction.
Grid-fed electric-motor liquefaction with no on-site gas-fired generation of any kind; no electricity-generation asset for GOGPT to track.
No captive generation or drive technology was ever disclosed, and the project was cancelled before reaching a design stage where such details are published.
Grid-electricity consumer; only combustion equipment in the record is temporary construction-phase diesel.
